paths.description: Homepage and live market dashboard, the primary landing and price-checking journey.
Currency market listing, representing dense market tables and category navigation.
News listing, representing editorial discovery and content navigation.
A stale article URL returning the site 404 template, used to judge failure and recovery UI.

findings.summary: System dark preference does not activate the site dark theme
findings.evidence: The dark-emulated screenshot is visually identical to the light capture, and the captured CSS contains no prefers-color-scheme or color-scheme declaration.
findings.suggestedFix: Add color-scheme: light dark and bind the existing dark palette to prefers-color-scheme, while retaining a manual override.

findings.summary: Long-running motion remains active under reduced-motion
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe reports roughly 100 running animations, including durations of 8s, 100s, and 1.7s, even though the media query matches.
findings.suggestedFix: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, stop marquees, pulsing indicators, and auto-advancing sliders rather than merely limiting one marquee iteration.

findings.summary: Important controls and market values fail contrast requirements
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility found multiple failures, including 1.02:1 download text, 3.05:1 indicator-button text, and 4.47:1 market values.
findings.suggestedFix: Use contrast-safe design tokens for text and controls in normal and high-contrast modes; verify all states at WCAG AA.

findings.summary: Route changes use abrupt full-page swaps
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection found no view-transition rules on a multi-route site; navigation between the dashboard, market, and news templates therefore has no continuity cue.
findings.suggestedFix: Add cross-document View Transitions for same-origin route changes with a no-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Fixed navigation does not communicate scroll progress or state
findings.evidence: Long pages reach 16,484px and 17,571px on mobile, while screenshots and CSS show fixed chrome but no scroll-state query or progress affordance.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight reading/scroll progress affordance and reduce sticky chrome after the user scrolls.

findings.summary: Custom menus and overlays lack anchor-aware positioning
findings.evidence: The DOM contains 24 modal/popup class occurrences but no anchor positioning rules, popover elements, or position-try fallback.
findings.suggestedFix: Use popover plus CSS anchor positioning and position-try fallbacks for transient menus and tooltips.

findings.summary: A notification opt-in modal obscures the primary content on every audited entry page
findings.evidence: Desktop, mobile, news, currency, and 404 captures all open with a large market-alert prompt covering the header and first content.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not open the opt-in prompt on page load. Ask after a relevant user action, make decline visually equal, and persist dismissal.

findings.summary: The blocking overlay is custom rather than a semantic dialog
findings.evidence: DOM evidence contains no dialog, popover, or details elements but 24 modal/popup class matches and seven onclick div/span controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement the modal with <dialog>, a labelled heading/description, focus management, Escape handling, and a real close button.

findings.summary: Advertising and fixed chrome dominate the first viewport
findings.evidence: The mobile first viewport is mostly a blocking modal, four banner ads, and fixed navigation; primary market content starts far below the header.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove or defer low-value banners and reserve the first viewport for current market data and clear navigation.

findings.summary: Responsive behavior is viewport-only
findings.evidence: The captured 39KB CSS has extensive viewport media queries but no @container rule, despite cards and tables being reused at multiple widths.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable cards/tables containment and adapt them with container queries rather than adding more global breakpoints.

findings.summary: Clickable non-controls weaken keyboard and touch predictability
findings.evidence: DOM inspection found seven div/span elements with onclick; Lighthouse also found icon links without accessible text, so non-pointer interaction is not consistently exposed.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace clickable div/span elements with button or anchor elements and provide visible :focus-visible styles and accessible names.

findings.summary: Measured load performance is poor
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured LCP 14.9s, CLS 1.031, TBT 560ms, and a performance score of 0.19. The narrow layout probe independently measured CLS 0.177.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile LCP discovery, reserve all dynamic space, and break up startup work until LCP and CLS reach good thresholds.

findings.summary: Late content causes substantial layout shift
findings.evidence: The layout observer recorded seven shifts totaling 0.177 on mobile; Lighthouse recorded CLS 1.031. All 63 inspected images lack explicit dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Set width/height or aspect-ratio on every image/ad slot and reserve stable space for asynchronously populated widgets and fonts.

findings.summary: Startup scripting repeatedly blocks the main thread
findings.evidence: The trace found eight long tasks, a 120ms longest task, and 249ms TBT; Lighthouse measured 560ms TBT.
findings.suggestedFix: Split initialization into user-visible chunks, yield between tasks, and delay analytics/widgets until idle or interaction.

findings.summary: The initial page is network-heavy and image-dominated
findings.evidence: HAR captured 84 requests and 5.56MB transferred, including 4.28MB across 57 images and seven font requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize only the actual LCP resource; lazy-load below-fold assets, consolidate fonts, and set long-lived immutable caching for versioned assets.

findings.summary: Large amounts of unused CSS and JavaScript ship at startup
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 260KiB unused CSS and 210KiB unused JavaScript, including analytics bundles and a stylesheet that is 91.8% unused.
findings.suggestedFix: Split CSS/JS by template and load analytics and optional widgets conditionally after consent or interaction.

findings.summary: Icon links and images lack accessible names
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found multiple icon-only links without accessible text and the AI image without alt; the image audit found two missing alt values.
findings.suggestedFix: Add explicit accessible names to icon links and meaningful alt text, or empty alt for decorative images.

findings.summary: Text and controls have insufficient colour contrast
findings.evidence: Lighthouse contrast audit failed on download text, the indicator finder, and repeated market values, with ratios as low as 1.02:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Raise foreground/background contrast using shared tokens and test normal, dark, and high-contrast states.

findings.summary: Heading order and control semantics are inconsistent
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports an invalid H4 heading jump and unnamed focusable links; custom onclick elements further obscure keyboard order and role.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a logical heading hierarchy and native controls, then keyboard-walk each template with a persistent focus indicator.

findings.summary: The page throws an uncaught exception during load
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured Uncaught TypeError in flickity.pkgd.js while reading option.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix or update the Flickity integration and add production error monitoring that preserves actionable stack context.

findings.summary: Images omit intrinsic dimensions and responsive delivery
findings.evidence: The image audit found missing dimensions on all 63 images, 19 oversized images, 25 without srcset, and 38 legacy-format images.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare intrinsic dimensions and srcset/sizes, then serve AVIF/WebP variants at the rendered size.

findings.summary: The page cannot use the back/forward cache
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports a BFCache failure because the page keeps a WebSocket connection open.
findings.suggestedFix: Close or suspend the WebSocket on pagehide and restore it on pageshow so history navigation can use BFCache.

findings.summary: The homepage has no useful meta description
findings.evidence: The rendered title is descriptive, but DOM inspection shows an empty meta description and Lighthouse fails meta-description.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a concise, unique Persian meta description for each template based on visible page content.

findings.summary: Several navigation actions are not crawlable links
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found javascript:void(0) anchors for analyses, contact, and support. Robots and viewport checks pass.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real href destinations for navigation and buttons for in-page actions, retaining descriptive visible link text.

findings.summary: CSP and analytics-cookie protections are too weak
findings.evidence: CSP only upgrades insecure requests, while two Google Analytics cookies are non-Secure, SameSite=None, and retained for 400 days.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive nonce/hash CSP and mark required cookies Secure with appropriate SameSite and shorter retention.

findings.summary: Tracking runs broadly before demonstrated consent
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence found 11 third-party origins and Google Tag Manager, DoubleClick, and Microsoft Clarity; the page sets 400-day analytics cookies.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate non-essential analytics behind informed consent, remove redundant trackers, shorten retention, and batch only necessary events.

findings.summary: Key browser-enforced defenses are absent
findings.evidence: Headers evidence reports no nosniff, frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy; CSP contains no script restrictions.
findings.suggestedFix: Add nosniff, frame-ancestors, strict Referrer-Policy, a minimal Permissions-Policy, and a restrictive CSP.

findings.summary: Custom overlay behavior dominates all route states
findings.evidence: The same custom blocking modal appears over the dashboard, news listing, currency listing, and 404 template instead of adapting to page state.
findings.suggestedFix: Persist the dismissed state and render route chrome only after stable state is known; use semantic top-layer primitives.

findings.summary: The 404 state offers little contextual recovery
findings.evidence: The stale article URL shows a generic “Oops! 404” illustration while the global alert still obscures the header; no contextual explanation or suggested news destinations are visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a clear Persian explanation, search, links to recent news and the originating category, while suppressing unrelated prompts.

findings.summary: The alert opt-in is a repeated nag on arrival
findings.evidence: Every route presents a yes/no market-alert prompt before the user has requested alerts or seen the underlying information.
findings.suggestedFix: Ask for alerts only after explicit interest, explain delivery/privacy, remember decline, and keep accept/decline equally prominent.

findings.summary: Inputs expose no autocomplete guidance
findings.evidence: DOM inspection found six inputs/selects/textareas and zero autocomplete attributes.
findings.suggestedFix: Add purpose-appropriate autocomplete tokens to search, contact, sign-in, and profile inputs; use off only where genuinely necessary.

findings.summary: Image delivery wastes bandwidth
findings.evidence: Images account for 4.28MB of the 5.56MB load; 38 are legacy GIF/PNG/JPEG, 19 are oversized, and 25 lack responsive sources.
findings.suggestedFix: Convert static imagery to AVIF/WebP, replace animated GIF ads with efficient video where allowed, and deliver responsive sizes.

findings.summary: Optional background and analytics work competes with the core page
findings.evidence: The trace records eight long tasks and the HAR/trackers evidence shows multiple analytics systems and live background endpoints on initial load.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer optional work until idle/consent, pause it when hidden, and consolidate live updates and analytics batches.

findings.summary: Ads, trackers, fonts, and animated media exceed a proportionate budget
findings.evidence: The first viewport is ad-heavy; the page transfers 5.56MB, contacts 11 third-party origins, and uses many animated GIF advertisements.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a per-template third-party/media budget, defer below-fold ads, remove duplicate analytics, and avoid autoplay animation by default.

findings.summary: Useful market capabilities are not exposed as structured agent actions
findings.evidence: The site has machine-readable server HTML and an AI affordance, but DOM inspection found no agentic forms or WebMCP tool registration.
findings.suggestedFix: For supported browsers, expose read-only price lookup and news search as narrowly scoped WebMCP tools with explicit user confirmation for state changes.

findings.summary: The long-lived dashboard could not complete a post-interaction heap capture
findings.evidence: A baseline heap completed, but after ten representative end-to-end scroll cycles the post heap did not complete within 300 seconds. This is low-confidence evidence of severe session degradation, not a confirmed retention slope.
findings.suggestedFix: Instrument live-update listeners/timers, repeat the interaction with baseline/target/final snapshots, and eliminate retained growth before shipping.

findings.summary: The homepage has a disproportionate in-memory footprint
findings.evidence: The baseline heap summary reports 954,692 nodes, 3,198,121 edges, and 61.5MB self size for a price/news dashboard.
findings.suggestedFix: Virtualize or omit hidden widgets, release unused data and DOM, and lazy-initialize sections outside the viewport.

taskList.title: Stop the on-load alert interruption and rebuild it as an in-context semantic dialog
Fix Core Web Vitals by reserving dynamic space and prioritising the actual LCP content
Cut image, ad, and third-party transfer cost
Repair accessible names, contrast, headings, and native control semantics
Deploy a restrictive CSP and complete defensive header/cookie policy
Reduce DOM/heap footprint and perform a conclusive repeated-interaction leak trace
